522	/// The bar's left-edge identity block: a kind-tinted chip, the selected clip's
523	/// name, and the track and kind under it.
524	///
525	/// It is one of three views of one selection — the timeline's own outline and
526	/// the inspector's header are the others — so its chip, its word for a kind
527	/// and its tint all come from `ClipKindStyle` rather than being spelled again
528	/// here.
529	///
530	/// Its width is FIXED at the design's 176 pt minimum rather than growing with
531	/// the name: the point of the block is that the divider after it never moves,
532	/// so a long name truncates instead of pushing the tools sideways.
533	final class TimelineSelectionBlock: NSView {
534	    private var snapshot = ProjectSnapshot.empty
535	    private var selection: Set<UInt32> = []
536	
537	    private static let width: CGFloat = 176
538	    private static let chip = NSSize(width: 8, height: 20)
539	    private static let gap: CGFloat = 8
540	
541	    init() {
542	        super.init(frame: .zero)
543	    }
544	
545	    @available(*, unavailable)
546	    required init?(coder: NSCoder) {
547	        fatalError("TimelineSelectionBlock does not support NSCoder")
548	    }
549	
550	    override var isFlipped: Bool { true }
551	
552	    override var intrinsicContentSize: NSSize {
553	        NSSize(width: Self.width, height: 30)
554	    }
555	
556	    func update(snapshot: ProjectSnapshot, selection: Set<UInt32>) {
557	        self.snapshot = snapshot
558	        self.selection = selection
559	        needsDisplay = true
560	    }
561	
562	    /// The clips the block is describing, in timeline order.
563	    private var clips: [ClipSnapshot] {
564	        snapshot.clips.filter { selection.contains($0.id) }.sorted { $0.start < $1.start }
565	    }
566	
567	    /// Chip tint, headline and meta line for the current selection.
568	    ///
569	    /// The design covers none and one. For MANY the honest thing is the count
570	    /// plus whatever the clips still agree on: a shared track keeps its name
571	    /// and a shared kind keeps its word, and where they disagree the line says
572	    /// so ("3 tracks", "mixed") rather than naming one clip's and implying it
573	    /// holds for the rest.
574	    private func description() -> (tint: NSColor, name: String, meta: String) {
575	        let clips = self.clips
576	        guard let first = clips.first else {
577	            return (DS.borderStrong, "No selection", "")
578	        }
579	        let kinds = Set(clips.map { ClipKindStyle.name(for: $0, in: snapshot) })
580	        let tracks = Set(clips.map { $0.track })
581	        let kind = kinds.count == 1 ? ClipKindStyle.name(for: first, in: snapshot) : "mixed"
582	        let track =
583	            tracks.count == 1 ? trackName(first.track) : "\(tracks.count) tracks"
584	        guard clips.count > 1 else {
585	            return (
586	                ClipKindStyle.tint(for: first, in: snapshot), snapshot.name(of: first),
587	                "\(track) · \(kind)")
588	        }
589	        let tint = kinds.count == 1
590	            ? ClipKindStyle.tint(for: first, in: snapshot) : DS.borderStrong
591	        return (tint, "\(clips.count) clips", "\(track) · \(kind)")
592	    }
593	
594	    /// The label a track wears in the timeline — the header column's spelling,
595	    /// not a second one.
596	    ///
597	    /// `set_track` accepts an EMPTY name, so `track(_:)?.name` is not enough:
598	    /// an unnamed track would print as nothing at all here while
599	    /// `TimelineHeaderView.draw` shows it as "Track 3", and the block would be
600	    /// naming a row the user cannot find. The number is the MODEL index + 1,
601	    /// which is what the header counts (0 = back), never the display row.
602	    private func trackName(_ id: UInt32) -> String {
603	        guard let index = snapshot.trackIndex(of: id) else { return "Track" }
604	        let name = snapshot.tracks[index].name
605	        return name.isEmpty ? "Track \(index + 1)" : name
606	    }
607	
608	    override func draw(_ dirtyRect: NSRect) {
609	        let content = description()
610	        let chip = NSRect(
611	            x: 0, y: (bounds.height - Self.chip.height) / 2,
612	            width: Self.chip.width, height: Self.chip.height)
613	        content.tint.setFill()
614	        chip.fill()
615	
616	        let textX = chip.maxX + Self.gap
617	        let textWidth = max(bounds.width - textX, 0)
618	        guard textWidth > 8 else { return }
619	        // The two lines are centred as a PAIR — 13 pt of name, 2 pt, 11 pt of
620	        // meta — so the block sits on the bar's centre line whatever height
621	        // the stack view hands it, and an empty meta line does not leave the
622	        // name floating high.
623	        let hasMeta = !content.meta.isEmpty
624	        let block: CGFloat = hasMeta ? 26 : 13
625	        let top = ((bounds.height - block) / 2).rounded()
626	        TimelineDraw.truncated(
627	            content.name,
628	            in: CGRect(x: textX, y: top, width: textWidth, height: 13),
629	            font: DS.sans(11, weight: .semibold), color: DS.textStrong)
630	        guard hasMeta else { return }
631	        TimelineDraw.truncated(
632	            content.meta,
633	            in: CGRect(x: textX, y: top + 15, width: textWidth, height: 11),
634	            font: DS.mono(9), color: DS.textFaint)
635	    }
636	}

4	/// The Media tab (spec §4.3): every imported file with its thumbnail, name,
5	/// duration, dimensions, rate and badges; Add Media… (⇧⌘I); Finder drops onto
6	/// the panel; a drag from a row to a timeline track or onto the canvas; the
7	/// find band road map 2's phase 8c added — a search, a sort and an "unused
8	/// only" switch (`MediaListFilter.swift`) — and the row menu: Insert at
9	/// Playhead, Overwrite at Playhead, Reveal in Timeline, Reveal in Finder,
10	/// Relink…, Remove.
11	///
12	/// There is no left panel in this app (§11), so this list IS the library.
13	/// Files are referenced, never copied (path + bookmark, §11), which is why a
14	/// row can be "missing" and why Relink… lives here.
15	///
16	/// **The find band does not rebuild the pane, and that is the whole design of
17	/// it.** `InspectorPaneView.rebuild()` removes every arranged subview and
18	/// asks `makeSections()` for a new set, `InspectorViewController.refresh` runs
19	/// it whenever `structureSignature` changes, and nothing in the inspector
20	/// preserves the first responder across one — so a search field built inside
21	/// `makeSections()` with the filtered set in the signature would be destroyed
22	/// by the first keystroke that changed the list, taking the field editor and
23	/// the caret with it (measured: removing a text field's ancestor leaves
24	/// `currentEditor()` nil and the window itself as first responder). So the
25	/// signature stays what it always was — a statement about the MODEL's shape —
26	/// and `arrange()` applies the search, the sort and the switch to the rows
27	/// that are already built, by hiding and re-ordering the list stack's
28	/// arranged subviews. Both are measured, not assumed: an `isHidden` arranged
29	/// subview leaves an `NSStackView`'s layout entirely (four 20 pt rows measure
30	/// 89 pt, three of them 66), and `insertArrangedSubview(_:at:)` MOVES a view
31	/// that is already arranged rather than duplicating it (the subview count
32	/// does not change) while leaving the window's first responder and the
33	/// caret's offset exactly where they were.
34	final class MediaPane: InspectorPaneView {
35	    override var tab: InspectorTab { .media }
36	
37	    /// The Media tab always has something to show — including when there is
38	    /// nothing imported yet, which is when Add Media… matters most.
39	    override var emptyMessage: String? { nil }
40	
41	    /// The rows, in the order the model lists them, each with the id it
42	    /// draws. The id is kept beside the view rather than read back off it so
43	    /// that `arrange()` can look the CURRENT entry up in the snapshot: a
44	    /// relink changes a file's name without changing this pane's signature,
45	    /// and a cached `MediaSnapshot` would sort and search against the name
46	    /// the row no longer shows.
47	    ///
48	    /// Internal rather than private for one caller: `select(_:)` redraws them
49	    /// and lives in `MediaPaneCommands.swift`, which is where the row's seven
50	    /// commands went when this file crossed the size cap. That is the whole
51	    /// cost of the split.
52	    var rows: [(media: UInt32, view: MediaRowView)] = []
53	
54	    /// The find band's state. View state, not persisted, and not part of the
55	    /// signature below — `MediaListFilter` argues both.
56	    private var filter = MediaListFilter()
57	
58	    /// The three things `arrange()` changes without a rebuild. Weak, because
59	    /// the view hierarchy owns them and a rebuild replaces all three;
60	    /// `InspectorPaneView.rebuild()` holds the previous generation one build
61	    /// longer, so a stale strong reference here would outlive the pane's own
62	    /// rule about that.
63	    private weak var listStack: NSStackView?
64	    private weak var tallyLabel: InspectorRowLabel?
65	    private weak var noMatchesRow: NSView?
66	
67	    /// The order `arrange()` last put the rows in, so it can leave the stack
68	    /// alone when nothing has moved — it runs on every refresh, and a live
69	    /// canvas drag refreshes this panel thirty times a second.
70	    private var arrangedOrder: [UInt32] = []
71	
72	    /// The MODEL's shape: which media exist and whether each one's file is
73	    /// there. Deliberately says nothing about the search text, the sort or
74	    /// the unused-only switch — see the class doc: putting the filtered set
75	    /// in here is precisely the bug this pane is built to avoid.
76	    override var structureSignature: String {
77	        // `:c` for a media with a cursor file: a Locate… or a Remove adds or
78	        // drops it, so the Cursor section's rows are rebuilt (CU-54).
79	        let media = binding.snapshot.media.map { entry -> String in
80	            "\(entry.id):\(mediaURL(for: entry) == nil ? "missing" : "ok")"
81	                + (entry.cursor == nil ? "" : ":c")
82	        }
83	        return "media|" + media.joined(separator: ",")
84	    }
85	
86	    override init(inspector: InspectorViewController) {
87	        super.init(inspector: inspector)
88	        // Finder drops land on the panel (§4.3). The editor's root view takes
89	        // file drops too, but it OPENS them as documents; a drop on this
90	        // panel means "add to this project", so the pane claims the type
91	        // first by being the deeper registered view.
92	        registerForDraggedTypes([.fileURL])
93	        NotificationCenter.default.addObserver(
94	            self, selector: #selector(cacheChanged(_:)), name: .mediaCacheDidChange, object: nil)
95	    }
96	
97	    @available(*, unavailable)
98	    required init?(coder: NSCoder) {
99	        fatalError("MediaPane does not support NSCoder")
100	    }
101	
102	    deinit {
103	        NotificationCenter.default.removeObserver(self)
104	    }
105	
106	    // MARK: - Sections
107	
108	    /// The redesign makes this tab a real LIST rather than a stack of button
109	    /// rows (handoff README, Part 2 §5): a 38 pt action row, the rows 3 pt
110	    /// apart, and a 40 pt footer carrying Consolidate… and one line saying
111	    /// what it does. It is still ONE `InspectorSection`, because the panel's
112	    /// shell builds every pane from sections and this one has no business
113	    /// forking that.
114	    override func makeSections() -> [InspectorSection] {
115	        rows = []
116	        listStack = nil
117	        noMatchesRow = nil
118	        arrangedOrder = []
119	        var content: [NSView] = [actionRow()]
120	        if binding.snapshot.media.isEmpty {
121	            // No find band with nothing to find: the band would be three dead
122	            // controls over a line saying the list is empty, and the pane is
123	            // rebuilt the moment the first file lands.
124	            content.append(
125	                inspectorRow(nil, [InspectorRowLabel("Drop files here, or use Add Media….")]))
126	        } else {
127	            content.append(findRow())
128	            content.append(listView())
129	            content.append(noMatchesView())
130	        }
131	        content.append(footerRow())
132	        // The rows exist and the band's controls hold the state, so the
133	        // filter can be applied to this build before it is ever shown — which
134	        // is what carries a search across the rebuild an import causes.
135	        arrange()
136	        let files = InspectorSection(id: "media.files", title: "Media", rows: content)
137	        // Camera Log (spec §11 GR-16) acts on a video file, so it is there
138	        // once the project has one (`MediaPane+CameraLog.swift`); HDR10 (spec
139	        // §11 HD-12) on a PQ file, once the project has one
140	        // (`MediaPane+HDR10.swift`); Cursor (spec §11 CU-54) on a video with a
141	        // picture, once the project has one (`MediaPane+Cursor.swift`).
142	        let media = binding.documentSnapshot.media
143	        let video = media.contains { $0.kind == .video }
144	        let pq = media.contains { $0.color?.pq != nil }
145	        let cursor = MediaPane.showsCursorSection(media)
146	        return (video ? [files, cameraLogSection()] : [files]) + (pq ? [hdr10Section()] : [])
147	            + (cursor ? [cursorSection()] : [])
148	    }
149	
150	    /// Add Media…, its ⇧⌘I hint, and the item count at the trailing edge.
151	    ///
152	    /// The count used to be a plain label built once per rebuild, because it
153	    /// changed only when the media list did. It changes with the FILTER now —
154	    /// "3 of 40 items" is the one line that stops a narrowed list reading as a
155	    /// lost library — so the label is held and `arrange()` writes it. It is
156	    /// still not an `OptionControl`: those read the model, and this reads the
157	    /// pane's own view state.
158	    private func actionRow() -> NSView {
159	        let add = commandButton(
160	            "Add Media…", #selector(EditorViewController.addMediaFiles(_:)),
161	            toolTip: "Import files into this project (⇧⌘I)")
162	
163	        let count = binding.snapshot.media.count
164	        let label = MediaPane.caption(MediaPane.tally(shown: count, of: count))
165	        tallyLabel = label

274	    /// this pane already holds — no rebuild, so the field being typed into
275	    /// keeps its caret (the class doc says why that is the point).
276	    ///
277	    /// The order is applied to EVERY row and the hiding to every row
278	    /// separately: moving a row and hiding one are different jobs, and a
279	    /// hidden row that keeps its place in the sort comes back where it
280	    /// belongs when the search is cleared. Nothing is written that does not
281	    /// have to be — this runs on every refresh, including a live gesture's
282	    /// thirty a second.
283	    private func arrange() {
284	        // The DOCUMENT's snapshot, and only one of the three things read off
285	        // it needs to be (road map 2's phase 9): `filter.admits` asks
286	        // `usesMedia`, and inside a nest a scoped view holds the NEST's clips
287	        // at top level and the timeline's nowhere — so a file used only by a
288	        // timeline clip would read as unused and "Unused only" would offer to
289	        // remove it. `media` itself is the same list either way (the view
290	        // carries the parent's `media[]` unchanged), so the order and the
291	        // tally are unaffected; this is written as one local so the question
292	        // cannot be asked two ways in one method.

295	        if let stack = listStack, order != arrangedOrder {
296	            var index = 0
297	            for id in order {
298	                guard let row = rows.first(where: { $0.media == id })?.view else { continue }

431	    ) -> NSView {
432	        let row = NSView()
433	        let bar = BarView(border: border)
434	        bar.translatesAutoresizingMaskIntoConstraints = false
435	        row.addSubview(bar)
436	        let rows = lines.map { views -> NSStackView in
437	            let line = NSStackView(views: views)
438	            line.orientation = .horizontal
439	            line.alignment = .centerY
440	            line.spacing = 8
441	            return line
442	        }

452	            // the same trailing edge and a flexible field on another fills the
453	            // same width.
454	            for line in rows {
455	                line.widthAnchor.constraint(equalTo: column.widthAnchor).isActive = true
456	            }
457	            stack = column
458	        }
459	        stack.translatesAutoresizingMaskIntoConstraints = false
460	        bar.addSubview(stack)
461	        let inset = InspectorMetrics.inset
462	        NSLayoutConstraint.activate([
463	            row.heightAnchor.constraint(equalToConstant: height),
464	            bar.topAnchor.constraint(equalTo: row.topAnchor),
465	            bar.bottomAnchor.constraint(equalTo: row.bottomAnchor),
466	            bar.leadingAnchor.constraint(equalTo: row.leadingAnchor, constant: -inset),
467	            bar.trailingAnchor.constraint(equalTo: row.trailingAnchor, constant: inset),
468	            stack.leadingAnchor.constraint(equalTo: bar.leadingAnchor, constant: inset),
469	            stack.trailingAnchor.constraint(equalTo: bar.trailingAnchor, constant: -inset),
470	            stack.centerYAnchor.constraint(equalTo: bar.centerYAnchor),
471	        ])

473	    }

507	/// The seven commands a media row calls back into, and the one question it
508	/// asks: `drop`, `select`, `place`, `revealInTimeline`, `reveal` (in Finder),
509	/// `relink` and `remove`, plus `canRevealInTimeline`.
510	///
511	/// **Why they are a file of their own.** Every one of them applies an edit
512	/// through `binding`, or writes the document's view state, or puts a panel or
513	/// an alert up — which is the pane's business and never a row's
514	/// (`MediaRowView.swift` argues that half) — and none of them touches the
515	/// list's views except `select`, which redraws them. So they are a seam, not
516	/// an amputation: what is left in `MediaPane.swift` is the LIST — its one
517	/// section, its three chrome bands, the find band's arrangement and the Finder
518	/// drop onto the panel.
519	///
520	/// The cut is road map 2's phase 8c paying the ~600-line rule a second time
521	/// for this pane. The first payment (commit b189ac3) moved the row and its
522	/// drag out at 822 lines, precisely so this phase's four additions would have
523	/// room; the additions cost more than the room left, as phase 6 warned they
524	/// would ("budget the cut against the pessimistic number"). It costs ONE
525	/// widening — `MediaPane.rows`, which `select` redraws — which is the toll
526	/// `ExporterLoudness.swift` records for splitting a type across files, and it
527	/// is the whole of it, because everything else here was already internal for
528	/// the row to call.
529	extension MediaPane {
530	    /// Where a dragged row landed. Returns false when the drop is refused, so
531	    /// the drag springs back rather than silently doing nothing.
532	    func drop(_ media: UInt32, on destination: NSView, target: MediaDropTarget) -> Bool {
533	        // A drag started in ANOTHER document's panel must not edit this one:
534	        // the session carries the source row, and the two windows differ.
535	        guard destination.window === window, window != nil else { return false }
536	        guard binding.snapshot.media(media) != nil else { return false }
537	        let fps = binding.canvas.fps
538	        switch target {
539	        case .track(let track, let at, let mode):
540	            let when = ReelTime.snapToFrame(max(at, 0), fps: fps)
541	            switch mode {
542	            case .add:
543	                binding.apply("Add Clip", [.addClip(track: track, media: media, at: when)])
544	            case .insert:
545	                binding.apply("Insert", [.insertClip(track: track, media: media, at: when)])
546	            case .overwrite:
547	                binding.apply(
548	                    "Overwrite", [.overwriteClip(track: track, media: media, at: when)])
549	            }
550	        case .canvas:
551	            let at = ReelTime.snapToFrame(max(binding.playhead, 0), fps: fps)
552	            let index = binding.snapshot.tracks.count
553	            // `add_track` returns a project, not an id (§11's one entry
554	            // point), so the id is learned from a PURE trial application
555	            // before the real edit runs.
556	            let existing = Set(binding.snapshot.tracks.map { $0.id })
557	            let probed = inspector?.onProbe?([.addTrack(index: index)])
558	            guard let track = probed?.tracks.first(where: { !existing.contains($0.id) })?.id else {
559	                guard let top = binding.snapshot.tracks.last?.id else { return false }
560	                binding.apply("Add Clip", [.addClip(track: top, media: media, at: at)])
561	                return true
562	            }
563	            binding.apply(
564	                "Add Clip",
565	                [.addTrack(index: index), .addClip(track: track, media: media, at: at)])
566	        }
567	        return true
568	    }

672	    /// agent's `relink_media` (`AgentServer.relinkMedia`) probes and passes
673	    /// the same way. What the pass costs is its own doc's: a stat, a marker
674	    /// read per half and a `fileExists` per media whose marker still matches,
675	    /// and a rebuild for the one whose file just changed.
676	    func relink(_ media: UInt32) {
677	        guard let entry = binding.snapshot.media(media), let window = window else {
678	            NSSound.beep()
679	            return
680	        }
681	        let binding = self.binding
682	        let panel = NSOpenPanel()
683	        panel.allowsMultipleSelection = false
684	        panel.canChooseDirectories = false
685	        panel.message = "Choose the file for “\(entry.name)”."
686	        panel.beginSheetModal(for: window) { response in
687	            guard response == .OK, let url = panel.url else { return }
688	            binding.document?.relinkMedia([(media: media, url: url)])
689	        }
690	    }

692	    /// Remove — refused while the media is in use, with the "and its clips"
693	    /// offer §4.3 asks for.
694	    ///
695	    /// The users are counted through `clipsUsing`, which walks the NESTS as
696	    /// well as the timeline, because that is the set `remove_media` refuses
697	    /// against and the set `with_clips: true` deletes. Filtering
698	    /// `snapshot.clips` here — what this line used to do — meant that media
699	    /// used only inside a compound clip looked unused, went to the core as a
700	    /// plain `remove_media`, came back refused, and reached the user as a
701	    /// beep with the alert never shown (`MediaUsage.swift`).
702	    func remove(_ media: UInt32) {
703	        guard let entry = binding.snapshot.media(media) else {
704	            NSSound.beep()
705	            return
706	        }
707	        // The DOCUMENT's clips, never the scoped view's: `remove_media` is a
708	        // document-level op (`ReelOp.isDocumentLevel`) and is sent unscoped
709	        // even with a nest open, so the "and its clips" count has to be the
710	        // whole file's — the timeline's clips chained with every nest's —
711	        // or the alert would under-count and the op would refuse.
712	        let users = binding.documentSnapshot.clipsUsing(media)
713	        // A LUT that is a media's Camera Log (spec §11 GR-16) is used too:
714	        // `with_clips` clears those conversions with the looks.
715	        let converted = entry.kind == .lut
716	            ? binding.documentSnapshot.mediaConverted(by: media).count : 0
717	        guard !users.isEmpty || converted > 0 else {
718	            binding.apply("Remove Media", [.removeMedia(media: media)])
719	            return
720	        }
721	        guard let window = window else {
722	            NSSound.beep()
723	            return
724	        }
725	        let binding = self.binding
726	        let alert = NSAlert()
727	        alert.messageText = "Remove “\(entry.name)”?"
728	        // A LUT's users keep their place and lose the look (spec §11 GR-8),
729	        // and the files it converts lose their Camera Log (GR-16).
730	        if entry.kind == .lut {
731	            var parts: [String] = []
732	            if !users.isEmpty {
733	                parts.append(
734	                    users.count == 1
735	                        ? "It is the look of 1 clip, which keeps its place and loses the look."
736	                        : "It is the look of \(users.count) clips, which keep their place and "
737	                            + "lose the look.")
738	            }
739	            if converted > 0 {
740	                parts.append(
741	                    (users.isEmpty ? "It is" : "…and")
742	                        + " the Camera Log of \(converted) file\(converted == 1 ? "" : "s"), "
743	                        + "which lose\(converted == 1 ? "s" : "") it.")
744	            }
745	            alert.informativeText = parts.joined(separator: " ")
746	        } else {
747	            alert.informativeText =
748	                users.count == 1
749	                ? "It is used by 1 clip, which will be removed with it."
750	                : "It is used by \(users.count) clips, which will be removed with it."
751	        }
752	        alert.addButton(
753	            withTitle: entry.kind == .lut ? "Remove and Clear Looks" : "Remove and Delete Clips")
754	        alert.addButton(withTitle: "Cancel")
755	        alert.beginSheetModal(for: window) { response in
756	            guard response == .alertFirstButtonReturn else { return }
757	            binding.applyGrouped(
758	                "Remove Media", [.removeMedia(media: media, withClips: true)])
759	        }
760	    }

764	/// How the Media tab's list is narrowed and ordered (road map 2's phase 8c):
765	/// a search over names, a sort, and the "unused only" switch.
766	///
767	/// A VALUE, in `AudioNormalize.swift`'s and `CaptionLayout.swift`'s shape —
768	/// media in, ids out — for the reason those two are values: the arithmetic is
769	/// then a function anybody can read, run and check without a panel, and the
770	/// pane above it does nothing but hand rows to the answer. It is also the
771	/// only way the ordering rules below can ever be measured, since a list of
772	/// rows in a scroll view is not something a proof script can interrogate.
773	///
774	/// **It is view state and it is not persisted**, which is a decision rather
775	/// than an omission. Three arguments, in the order they were made:
776	/// a search is an act of FINDING and not a preference, and a panel that comes
777	/// back tomorrow showing two of a project's forty files — because of what
778	/// somebody typed once — is a bug report about missing media; the pane is
779	/// rebuilt per document window, so two open projects filter independently,
780	/// which is what "the Media tab of THIS project" means; and a `UserDefaults`
781	/// key would have to be pinned in the offscreen harness's `pinDefaults` or
782	/// every chrome render of this pane would depend on whatever the machine
783	/// happened to store (app/CLAUDE.md's rule for the keys the chrome reads).
784	/// Nothing here writes a default and nothing reads one.
785	struct MediaListFilter: Equatable {
786	    /// The sort popup's rows, in menu order; the raw value IS the row index,
787	    /// so the order is API for the popup that reads it.
788	    ///
789	    /// **`importOrder` is spelled "Import Order" and not "Added"**, which the
790	    /// road map's own wording ("name, duration, added, kind") would have
791	    /// suggested, because the app knows an ORDER and does not know a TIME.
792	    /// Nothing records when a media entry arrived: `MediaSnapshot` and the
793	    /// core's `Media` are the same eleven keys and none of them is a
794	    /// timestamp. What the media array carries instead is insertion order —
795	    /// `add_media` pushes after `allocate_id` (`core/src/edit_track.rs`),
796	    /// `absorb_media` does the same (`edit_paste.rs`), `remove_media` retains
797	    /// and `relink_media` mutates in place, so nothing ever reorders it — and
798	    /// for any project built by ops that is also ascending id order. A real
799	    /// "date added" would be a persisted field, which is a version-7 schema
800	    /// bump, and phase 8 is declared "no schema; view state throughout": a
801	    /// row that says what the app actually knows is worth more than a row
802	    /// that says what the road map wished it knew.
803	    enum Order: Int, CaseIterable {
804	        case importOrder, name, duration, kind
805	
806	        var title: String {
807	            switch self {
808	            case .importOrder: return "Import Order"
809	            case .name: return "Name"
810	            case .duration: return "Duration"
811	            case .kind: return "Kind"
812	            }
813	        }
814	    }
815	
816	    /// What was typed in the search field, verbatim. Not trimmed: the field
817	    /// is on screen beside the list, and a filter that quietly ignored a
818	    /// space somebody typed would disagree with what they can see. Empty is
819	    /// the only value that means "no search".
820	    var search = ""
821	    var order = Order.importOrder
822	    var unusedOnly = false
823	
824	    /// Whether the list is showing less than the project holds — what the
825	    /// item count says out loud, so "3 of 40 items" never appears over a
826	    /// list that is showing everything.
827	    var isNarrowing: Bool { !search.isEmpty || unusedOnly }
828	
829	    /// Whether one entry survives the two filters.
830	    ///
831	    /// The name test is `localizedStandardContains`, which is the comparison
832	    /// Finder searches with: case-insensitive, diacritic-insensitive and
833	    /// width-insensitive against the current locale, so `resume` finds
834	    /// `Résumé.mov` and `KEYNOTE` finds `keynote.mov`. Spelling it out as
835	    /// `range(of:options:)` would be the same three options with a fourth
836	    /// chance to forget one.
837	    ///
838	    /// "Unused" is `ProjectSnapshot.usesMedia`, which walks the nests as well
839	    /// as the timeline (`MediaUsage.swift`) — so a file that appears only
840	    /// inside a compound clip is USED and is not offered up for deletion by
841	    /// this filter, which is exactly what `remove_media` will say if it is
842	    /// asked.
843	    func admits(_ entry: MediaSnapshot, in snapshot: ProjectSnapshot) -> Bool {
844	        if unusedOnly, snapshot.usesMedia(entry.id) { return false }
845	        guard !search.isEmpty else { return true }
846	        return entry.name.localizedStandardContains(search)
847	    }
848	
849	    /// The ids of `media` in the order the list should show them — every id,
850	    /// filtered or not, because hiding a row and moving it are two different
851	    /// jobs and the pane does them separately.
852	    ///
853	    /// **Every order is ascending and every tie falls back to import order**,
854	    /// which is one rule rather than four opinions: a list of a few dozen
855	    /// files reads as well from either end, and "longest first" versus
856	    /// "shortest first" is an argument with no answer that would then have to
857	    /// be re-had for kind. The tiebreak is not decoration —
858	    /// `Array.sort` is not documented stable, so without it two files of the
859	    /// same duration could swap places between two runs of the same sort,
860	    /// which is the kind of thing nobody reports and everybody notices.
861	    func ordered(_ media: [MediaSnapshot]) -> [UInt32] {
862	        guard order != .importOrder else { return media.map { $0.id } }
863	        return media.enumerated().sorted { a, b in
864	            switch order {
865	            case .importOrder:
866	                return a.offset < b.offset
867	            case .name:
868	                let compared = a.element.name.localizedStandardCompare(b.element.name)
869	                if compared == .orderedSame { return a.offset < b.offset }
870	                return compared == .orderedAscending
871	            case .duration:
872	                return a.element.duration == b.element.duration
873	                    ? a.offset < b.offset : a.element.duration < b.element.duration
874	            case .kind:
875	                let left = a.element.kind.displayName
876	                let right = b.element.kind.displayName
877	                return left == right ? a.offset < b.offset : left < right
878	            }
879	        }.map { $0.element.id }
880	    }
881	}

950	/// `controlTextDidEndEditing`, and `OptionFieldControl` is the same shape
951	/// with a number in it; all three are editing the MODEL, where a keystroke

957	/// (`MediaListFilter.search`); this field is handed the current one at build

959	/// value" rule the rest of the inspector is built on (`InspectorPane.swift`).
960	/// That matters for one reason beyond tidiness: the pane is REBUILT whenever
961	/// the media list changes, which destroys this view, and a search that lived
962	/// in the field would be lost with it while the list stayed narrowed.
963	///
964	/// Escape clears rather than reverting. AppKit's default for a text field is
965	/// to put back the value the field started editing with and end editing,
966	/// which for a search box means "undo my typing" where every other app on
967	/// this machine means "show me everything again".
968	///
969	/// **Not an `NSSearchField`**, though this is exactly what one is for: that
970	/// class draws its own bezel, magnifier and cancel button and would be the
971	/// only system-looking control in a panel whose every field is

973	/// and it sends its action on a TIMER by default, which is a second answer to
974	/// "when does the list narrow" living somewhere this file cannot see. What it
975	/// would have brought for free is the cancel button and the recent-searches
976	/// menu; the first is Escape here and the second is not wanted in a list of a

983	        super.init(frame: .zero)
984	        DSField.style(self, height: 24, radius: DS.controlRadius, font: DS.sans(11))

990	    @available(*, unavailable)

992	        fatalError("MediaSearchField does not support NSCoder")
993	    }

996	        changed(stringValue)
997	    }

1000	        _ control: NSControl, textView: NSTextView, doCommandBy commandSelector: Selector
1001	    ) -> Bool {
1002	        guard commandSelector == #selector(NSResponder.cancelOperation(_:)) else { return false }

1014	/// Reveal in Timeline's other half (road map 2's phase 8c): the Media tab
1015	/// picks the clips, and these two put them on screen.
1016	///
1017	/// The split is the usual one and it is not optional. A pane cannot reach the
1018	/// timeline — `EditorViewController`'s views are its own, and the inspector
1019	/// talks to the editor through `onCommand`, a bare `Selector` — so the pane
1020	/// writes the SELECTION (view state, the way it writes `selectedMedia`) and
1021	/// sends a command; the editor publishes it on the one document channel and
1022	/// asks the timeline to scroll. Nothing here is an op, nothing registers an
1023	/// undo step, and there is no MCP mirror to owe: `set_selection` has been the
1024	/// mirror of "the selection changed" since M2, and an agent that wants these
1025	/// clips selected already asks for them by id.
1026	extension EditorViewController {
1027	    /// The selection the Media tab just wrote, published and scrolled to.
1028	    ///
1029	    /// It publishes FIRST: `viewStateDidChange` is what pushes the new
1030	    /// selection into `TimelineView.update`, and scrolling to a clip the view
1031	    /// has not been told about yet would work by luck (the x mapping does not
1032	    /// depend on the selection today) and stop working the day it does.
1033	    ///
1034	    /// The clip it reveals is the EARLIEST — the first one the eye would look
1035	    /// for — with the lower id breaking a tie so that two clips starting
1036	    /// together always reveal the same one. `Array.min(by:)` is not
1037	    /// documented stable, which is exactly why the tiebreak is written down:
1038	    /// with it the answer is a total order and cannot depend on the sort.
1039	    /// (`paste_attributes` answers the same "several clips, one of them
1040	    /// first" question with a third term, the front-most track — it is
1041	    /// choosing a clip to COPY FROM, where the choice changes the result;
1042	    /// here two clips at one start are equally good to look at.)
1043	    @objc func revealSelectionInTimeline(_ sender: Any?) {
1044	        viewStateDidChange()
1045	        guard let document = document, let timeline = timeline else { return }
1046	        let selected = document.editedProject.snapshot.clips.filter {
1047	            document.selection.contains($0.id)
1048	        }
1049	        guard let first = selected.min(by: { ($0.start, $0.id) < ($1.start, $1.id) }) else {
1050	            return
1051	        }

1058	    /// position alone on whichever axis already shows it.
1059	    ///
1060	    /// **Horizontally this is `revealPlayhead`'s rule, deliberately**: the
1061	    /// same 24 pt margins and the same "put it 35 % in" landing, so a clip
1062	    /// found through the Media tab arrives where a clip the playhead ran onto
1063	    /// arrives. That is what `scroll(toX:)` had to widen from private for — a
1064	    /// widening this change forces, in the shape phase 1 set when
1065	    /// `dragSnapper` and `makeSnapper` widened for
1066	    /// `EditorViewController+Edge.swift`. The BODY stays out of the frozen
1067	    /// file; only the one word changed there.
1068	    ///
1069	    /// **Vertically it is `scrollToVisible`**, which needed no widening at
1070	    /// all: `content` is already internal (the media drop target in
1071	    /// `MediaRowView.swift` reaches it), and the minimum scroll that shows a
1072	    /// lane is the right answer for lanes — there is no "35 % down" to want.
1073	    /// The rect is grown UPWARD by the ruler's height because the ruler is a
1074	    /// floating subview pinned to the top of the visible rectangle: a lane
1075	    /// scrolled to sit flush with the top edge would sit UNDER it. The x range
1076	    /// asked for is exactly the one already visible, so this call can only
1077	    /// move the view vertically, and it goes first for that reason — the
1078	    /// horizontal step below then reads a `pinnedX` nothing has moved.
1079	    ///
1080	    /// A clip on a track this view has not been told about yet, or a viewport
1081	    /// with no size (before the first layout), is nothing to scroll to.
1082	    func reveal(_ clip: ClipSnapshot) {
1083	        guard let index = snapshot.tracks.firstIndex(where: { $0.id == clip.track }),
1084	              layout.viewport.width > 0
1085	        else { return }
1086	        let rect = layout.clipRect(clip, row: layout.row(forTrackIndex: index))
1087	
1088	        content.scrollToVisible(
1089	            CGRect(
1090	                x: pinnedX, y: rect.minY - TimelineLayout.rulerHeight,
1091	                width: layout.viewport.width, height: rect.height + TimelineLayout.rulerHeight))
1092	
1093	        let left = pinnedX + TimelineLayout.headerWidth + 24
1094	        let right = pinnedX + layout.viewport.width - 24
1095	        guard rect.minX < left || rect.minX > right else { return }
1096	        scroll(toX: rect.minX - TimelineLayout.headerWidth - layout.viewport.width * 0.35)
1097	    }

1	import AppKit

3	/// The window toolbar — the chrome cleanup's §1, and the whole of it.
4	///
5	/// **One job instead of four.** The 44 pt row keeps only what applies to the
6	/// document at all times: *where you are in it* (transport, timecode), *how
7	/// you are looking at it* (canvas zoom, safe guides) and *getting it out*
8	/// (Export). Everything that acts on a clip went down to the timeline bar,
9	/// next to blade and ripple-delete where it belongs — Add Text and Add Shape
10	/// moved, and the toolbar's Add Marker was a second copy of the one the
11	/// timeline bar already had, so it is simply gone. The `@objc` forwards for
12	/// all three stay in `EditorViewController.swift`: the menus still use them.
13	///
14	/// Split out of `EditorViewController` because that file is frozen at wiring
15	/// (app/CLAUDE.md). The seven stored views have to stay there — an extension
16	/// cannot add stored properties — which is exactly the case that file's header
17	/// makes for their being internal rather than private; everything that is only
18	/// behaviour is here.
19	extension EditorViewController {
20	    // MARK: - Metrics
21	
22	    /// The transport cluster's shared button geometry. Read from the frozen
23	    /// file's `playButton` / `pauseButton` / `loopButton` initialisers as well
24	    /// as from `buildToolbar`, so the six buttons cannot drift apart.
25	    ///
26	    /// **34, not the design's 30.** The handoff asks for 30 × 26 buttons AND a
27	    /// 19 pt symbol, and the two cannot both hold: `backward` and `forward` at
28	    /// pointSize 19 weight `.medium` measure exactly 30 × 18 pt (measured), so
29	    /// `GhostButton.drawIcon` centres them at x = 0 spanning the whole button
30	    /// — no side padding at all, and the glyph touches the hover fill's
31	    /// corners. 34 leaves 2 pt each side, which is what the narrower five
32	    /// (`backward.end`/`forward.end` 21, `play.fill` 18, `repeat` 26) already
33	    /// had, so all six keep one optical rhythm.
34	    static let transportButtonSize = NSSize(width: 34, height: 26)
35	    static let transportSymbolPointSize: CGFloat = 19
36	
37	    /// 12 pt of padding at both ends and 12 pt between clusters; 2 pt inside
38	    /// the transport, which reads as one control rather than six.
39	    private static let toolbarPadding: CGFloat = 12
40	    private static let toolbarClusterGap: CGFloat = 12
41	    private static let transportGap: CGFloat = 2
42	    /// The rule between clusters, and the timecode field's width — wide enough
43	    /// for `HH:MM:SS:FF` in mono 12.
44	    private static let toolbarDividerLength: CGFloat = 20
45	    private static let timecodeWidth: CGFloat = 112
46	
47	    // MARK: - Construction
48	
49	    /// Transport · timecode ——— view · Export. Called once, from `loadView`.
50	    func buildToolbar() -> NSView {
51	        let bar = BarView(border: .bottom)
52	
53	        // 24 pt on the button radius rather than the 26 pt field default: the
54	        // timecode sits in a row of 26 pt buttons and a taller field would be
55	        // the only thing out of line in it.
56	        DSField.style(
57	            timecodeField, height: 24, radius: DS.buttonRadius,
58	            font: DS.mono(12, weight: .medium))
59	        timecodeField.alignment = .center
60	        timecodeField.delegate = self
61	        timecodeField.toolTip = "Current time — click to type one (1:23, 83.5, 1:23:04)"
62	        timecodeField.widthAnchor.constraint(equalToConstant: Self.timecodeWidth).isActive = true
63	
64	        durationLabel.font = DS.mono(11)
65	        durationLabel.textColor = DS.textFaint
66	
67	        zoomPopup = OptionPopupControl(
68	            width: 74, items: Self.canvasZoomTitles,
69	            read: { [weak self] in self?.canvasZoomIndex ?? 0 },
70	            write: { [weak self] index in self?.setCanvasZoom(index) },
71	            enabled: { true },
72	            onEdit: { [weak self] in self?.refreshToolbarControls() })
73	
74	        safeToggle = OptionCheckboxControl(
75	            label: "Safe",
76	            read: { [weak self] in self?.safeGuidesVisible ?? false },
77	            write: { [weak self] value in self?.setSafeGuides(value) },
78	            enabled: { true },
79	            onEdit: { [weak self] in self?.refreshToolbarControls() })
80	
81	        let row = NSStackView(views: [
82	            transportCluster(),
83	            DividerView(length: Self.toolbarDividerLength),
84	            timecodeCluster(),
85	            flexibleSpace(),
86	            viewCluster(),
87	            DividerView(length: Self.toolbarDividerLength),
88	            AccentButton(
89	                title: "Export…", symbol: "square.and.arrow.up", fallback: "⤴",
90	                tooltip: "Export… (⌘E)", action: #selector(exportProject(_:))),
91	        ])
92	        row.translatesAutoresizingMaskIntoConstraints = false
93	        row.orientation = .horizontal
94	        row.alignment = .centerY
95	        row.spacing = Self.toolbarClusterGap
96	        bar.addSubview(row)
97	        NSLayoutConstraint.activate([
98	            row.leadingAnchor.constraint(
99	                equalTo: bar.leadingAnchor, constant: Self.toolbarPadding),
100	            row.trailingAnchor.constraint(
101	                equalTo: bar.trailingAnchor, constant: -Self.toolbarPadding),
102	            row.centerYAnchor.constraint(equalTo: bar.centerYAnchor),
103	        ])
104	        return bar
105	    }
106	
107	    /// Six buttons, one of which is the play/pause pair swapping on `isHidden`
108	    /// (`playbackRateChanged`) — so the cluster is always six wide and the
109	    /// timecode beside it never shifts when playback starts.
110	    private func transportCluster() -> NSStackView {
111	        let cluster = NSStackView(views: [
112	            transportButton(
113	                symbol: "backward.end", fallback: "⏮", tooltip: "Go to Start (Home)",
114	                action: #selector(goToStart(_:))),
115	            transportButton(
116	                symbol: "backward", fallback: "◀◀", tooltip: "Previous Edit Point (↑)",
117	                action: #selector(previousEditPoint(_:))),
118	            playButton, pauseButton,
119	            transportButton(
120	                symbol: "forward", fallback: "▶▶", tooltip: "Next Edit Point (↓)",
121	                action: #selector(nextEditPoint(_:))),
122	            transportButton(
123	                symbol: "forward.end", fallback: "⏭", tooltip: "Go to End (End)",
124	                action: #selector(goToEnd(_:))),
125	            loopButton,
126	        ])
127	        cluster.orientation = .horizontal
128	        cluster.spacing = Self.transportGap
129	        return cluster
130	    }
131	
132	    private func transportButton(
133	        symbol: String, fallback: String, tooltip: String, action: Selector
134	    ) -> GhostButton {
135	        GhostButton(
136	            symbol: symbol, fallback: fallback, caption: nil, tooltip: tooltip, action: action,
137	            size: Self.transportButtonSize, pointSize: Self.transportSymbolPointSize,
138	            cornerRadius: DS.buttonRadius)
139	    }
140	
141	    /// The position field and the document's duration after it. One cluster,
142	    /// because "83:04 of 00:00:37:05" is one fact.
143	    private func timecodeCluster() -> NSStackView {
144	        let cluster = NSStackView(views: [timecodeField, durationLabel])
145	        cluster.orientation = .horizontal
146	        cluster.alignment = .centerY
147	        cluster.spacing = 6
148	        return cluster
149	    }
150	
151	    private func viewCluster() -> NSStackView {
152	        let cluster = NSStackView(views: [zoomPopup, safeToggle])
153	        cluster.orientation = .horizontal
154	        cluster.alignment = .centerY
155	        cluster.spacing = 10
156	        return cluster
157	    }
158	
159	    /// The gap that pushes View and Export to the trailing edge. Priority 1 on
160	    /// both axes of resistance so the stack takes every spare point out of this
161	    /// view and none out of a control.
162	    private func flexibleSpace() -> NSView {
163	        let spacer = NSView()
164	        spacer.setContentHuggingPriority(NSLayoutConstraint.Priority(1), for: .horizontal)
165	        spacer.setContentCompressionResistancePriority(
166	            NSLayoutConstraint.Priority(1), for: .horizontal)
167	        return spacer
168	    }
169	
170	    // MARK: - Refresh
171	
172	    /// Pulls the two option controls back into agreement with the flags they
173	    /// read, and dims Loop when it is off — `GhostButton` has no on-state, and
174	    /// alpha is the whole of the toggle's state model here.
175	    func refreshToolbarControls() {
176	        zoomPopup?.refresh()
177	        safeToggle?.refresh()
178	        loopButton.alphaValue = loopEnabled ? 1 : 0.55
179	    }
180	}
181	import AppKit

183	// MARK: - BarView
184	
185	/// A chrome bar: the window background with a 1px hairline on one edge.
186	/// Frame Job's toolbar row (spec §3, 44 pt) and, later, the timeline's own
187	/// toolbar row are both this. Copied from Rasterize's `EditorChrome.swift` —
188	/// keep them in sync rather than forking.
189	final class BarView: NSView {
190	    enum Border {
191	        case top
192	        case bottom
193	        /// Both edges — the timeline bar, which has lanes under it and a
194	        /// split divider over it and needs to read as its own band. The one
195	        /// case Rasterize's copy does not have.
196	        case both
197	        case none
198	    }
199	
200	    private let border: Border
201	
202	    init(border: Border) {
203	        self.border = border
204	        super.init(frame: .zero)
205	    }
206	
207	    @available(*, unavailable)
208	    required init?(coder: NSCoder) {
209	        fatalError("BarView does not support NSCoder")
210	    }
211	
212	    override var isFlipped: Bool { true }
213	
214	    override func draw(_ dirtyRect: NSRect) {
215	        DS.chromeBackground.setFill()
216	        bounds.fill()
217	        DS.border.setFill()
218	        switch border {
219	        case .top:
220	            NSRect(x: 0, y: 0, width: bounds.width, height: 1).fill()
221	        case .bottom:
222	            NSRect(x: 0, y: bounds.height - 1, width: bounds.width, height: 1).fill()
223	        case .both:
224	            NSRect(x: 0, y: 0, width: bounds.width, height: 1).fill()
225	            NSRect(x: 0, y: bounds.height - 1, width: bounds.width, height: 1).fill()
226	        case .none:
227	            break
228	        }
229	    }
230	}
231	
232	// MARK: - SafeGuidesView
233	
234	/// The toolbar's Safe toggle (spec §4.1): the 90 % title-safe and 80 %
235	/// action-safe rectangles, drawn over the preview.
236	///
237	/// It is sized to the VIDEO rectangle by `EditorViewController.layoutCanvas`,
238	/// not to the pane, so the percentages are of the canvas and not of whatever
239	/// letterboxing is around it. Hit-transparent: the canvas overlay a later
240	/// stage puts here has to receive every click.
241	final class SafeGuidesView: NSView {
242	    override init(frame frameRect: NSRect) {
243	        super.init(frame: frameRect)
244	        wantsLayer = true
245	    }
246	
247	    @available(*, unavailable)
248	    required init?(coder: NSCoder) {
249	        fatalError("SafeGuidesView does not support NSCoder")
250	    }
251	
252	    override func hitTest(_ point: NSPoint) -> NSView? { nil }
253	
254	    override func draw(_ dirtyRect: NSRect) {
255	        guard bounds.width > 2, bounds.height > 2 else { return }
256	        let rings: [(fraction: CGFloat, alpha: CGFloat)] = [(0.9, 0.85), (0.8, 0.55)]
257	        for (fraction, alpha) in rings {
258	            let inset = NSRect(
259	                x: bounds.width * (1 - fraction) / 2,
260	                y: bounds.height * (1 - fraction) / 2,
261	                width: bounds.width * fraction,
262	                height: bounds.height * fraction)
263	            let path = NSBezierPath(rect: inset.insetBy(dx: 0.5, dy: 0.5))
264	            path.lineWidth = 1
265	            DS.marquee.withAlphaComponent(alpha).setStroke()
266	            path.stroke()
267	        }
268	    }
269	}
270	
271	// MARK: - PanePlaceholderView
272	
273	/// A labelled stand-in for a pane whose real content lands in a later stage
274	/// (the inspector's tabs, the timeline). It draws the pane's name and a one
275	/// line note so an unfinished build reads as unfinished rather than broken,
276	/// and it is replaced wholesale — the containers around it
277	/// (`EditorViewController.inspectorContainer` / `.timelineContainer`) are
278	/// what later stages fill.
279	final class PanePlaceholderView: NSView {
280	    private let name: String
281	    private let note: String
282	
283	    init(name: String, note: String) {
284	        self.name = name
285	        self.note = note
286	        super.init(frame: .zero)
287	        wantsLayer = true
288	    }
289	
290	    @available(*, unavailable)
291	    required init?(coder: NSCoder) {
292	        fatalError("PanePlaceholderView does not support NSCoder")
293	    }
294	
295	    override var isFlipped: Bool { true }
296	
297	    override func draw(_ dirtyRect: NSRect) {
298	        DS.chromeBackground.setFill()
299	        bounds.fill()
300	
301	        let title = DS.microLabel(name, size: 11)
302	        title.draw(at: NSPoint(x: 14, y: 12))
303	
304	        let attributes: [NSAttributedString.Key: Any] = [
305	            .font: DS.sans(12),
306	            .foregroundColor: DS.textFaint,
307	        ]
308	        note.draw(
309	            with: NSRect(x: 14, y: 34, width: max(bounds.width - 28, 10), height: 60),
310	            options: [.usesLineFragmentOrigin],
311	            attributes: attributes)
312	    }
313	}
314	import AppKit
315	
316	/// The 36 pt bar over the lanes (the redesign's §4): a fixed selection block
317	/// at the left edge that never moves, then the tools.
318	///
319	/// It mirrors Rasterize's options bar — identity first, then what acts on it.
320	/// Duplicate, Add Text and Add Shape came DOWN from the window toolbar in the
321	/// same change: they act on a clip, so they belong next to blade and ripple
322	/// delete rather than beside Export. Built here rather than in
323	/// `TimelineView.swift`, which is frozen at wiring (app/CLAUDE.md); the view
324	/// keeps only the three handles it later refreshes.
325	enum TimelineBar {
326	    /// What `TimelineView` has to hold on to after the bar is built: the
327	    /// block it pushes a selection into and the two option controls it asks
328	    /// to re-read themselves.
329	    ///
330	    /// The level meter is deliberately NOT here. It subscribes to
331	    /// `LevelMeter.shared` itself, so nothing has to push into it and the
332	    /// frozen `TimelineView` and `EditorViewController` gain neither a stored
333	    /// handle nor a fan-out line for it.
334	    struct Parts {
335	        let view: NSView
336	        let selection: TimelineSelectionBlock
337	        let snap: OptionCheckboxControl
338	        let size: OptionSegmentedControl
339	    }
340	
341	    /// The design's 12 pt edge padding and 12 pt between clusters.
342	    private static let padding: CGFloat = 12
343	    /// Edit-action buttons: 28 × 24 at 17 pt, on the square button radius.
344	    private static let actionSize = NSSize(width: 28, height: 24)
345	    private static let actionPointSize: CGFloat = 17
346	
347	    static func build(owner: TimelineView) -> Parts {
348	        let bar = BarView(border: .both)
349	
350	        let selection = TimelineSelectionBlock()
351	
352	        let actions = NSStackView(views: editActions())
353	        actions.orientation = .horizontal
354	        actions.spacing = 2
355	
356	        let snap = OptionCheckboxControl(
357	            label: "Snap",
358	            read: { [weak owner] in owner?.snappingEnabled ?? false },
359	            write: { [weak owner] _ in owner?.onSnappingToggled?() },
360	            enabled: { true },
361	            onEdit: { [weak owner] in owner?.snapToggle?.refresh() })
362	
363	        let size = OptionSegmentedControl(
364	            segments: [
365	                (symbol: "framejob.small", fallback: "S", tooltip: "Small tracks"),
366	                (symbol: "framejob.medium", fallback: "M", tooltip: "Medium tracks"),
367	                (symbol: "framejob.large", fallback: "L", tooltip: "Large tracks"),
368	            ],
369	            read: { [weak owner] in owner?.trackHeightIndex ?? 1 },
370	            write: { [weak owner] index in owner?.onTrackHeightChanged?(index) },
371	            segmentEnabled: nil, enabled: { true },
372	            onEdit: { [weak owner] in owner?.heightControl?.refresh() })
373	
374	        let spacer = NSView()
375	        spacer.setContentHuggingPriority(NSLayoutConstraint.Priority(1), for: .horizontal)
376	        spacer.setContentCompressionResistancePriority(
377	            NSLayoutConstraint.Priority(1), for: .horizontal)
378	
379	        // The meter goes in the flexible gap, immediately left of the zoom
380	        // cluster, rather than last: placing it after S/M/L would shift the
381	        // zoom cluster and the size control 130-odd points left, and both are
382	        // two phases of muscle memory old. Here nothing that shipped moves at
383	        // any window width, because the meter carries the spacer's own
384	        // priority-1 hugging and compression resistance and absorbs slack up
385	        // to its own cap.
386	        //
387	        // It gets NO divider before it, and that is arithmetic rather than
388	        // taste: the row's fixed content measures 880 pt against a 900 pt
389	        // minimum window, one more stack gap for the meter makes 892, and a
390	        // divider's second gap plus its hairline would make 905 — broken
391	        // constraints at the minimum window, which nothing in this project
392	        // asserts on and no proof would catch. The meter compresses to
393	        // nothing and stops drawing instead (`LevelMeterView.draw`).
394	        let row = NSStackView(views: [
395	            selection, DividerView(length: 18), actions, DividerView(length: 18), snap, spacer,
396	            LevelMeterView(), zoomCluster(owner: owner), DividerView(length: 18), size,
397	        ])
398	        row.translatesAutoresizingMaskIntoConstraints = false
399	        row.orientation = .horizontal
400	        row.alignment = .centerY
401	        row.spacing = padding
402	        bar.addSubview(row)
403	        NSLayoutConstraint.activate([
404	            row.leadingAnchor.constraint(equalTo: bar.leadingAnchor, constant: padding),
405	            row.trailingAnchor.constraint(equalTo: bar.trailingAnchor, constant: -padding),
406	            row.centerYAnchor.constraint(equalTo: bar.centerYAnchor),
407	        ])
408	        return Parts(view: bar, selection: selection, snap: snap, size: size)
409	    }
410	
411	    /// The eight actions, in the design's order. Every selector already exists
412	    /// on `EditorViewController` and every button dispatches through the
413	    /// responder chain, exactly as the old timeline toolbar did.
414	    ///
415	    /// The design lists seven; **Add Shape is the eighth and is deliberate**.
416	    /// Shape has no menu item anywhere in the app, so its toolbar button was
417	    /// the only way to reach the feature — dropping it with the rest of the
418	    /// window toolbar would have deleted a command, not moved one.
419	    private static func editActions() -> [NSView] {
420	        let items: [(String, String, String, Selector)] = [
421	            (
422	                "scissors", "✂", "Split (⌘T)",
423	                #selector(EditorViewController.splitAtPlayhead(_:))
424	            ),
425	            (
426	                "arrow.right.to.line", "⇥", "Trim Start to Playhead (W)",
427	                #selector(EditorViewController.trimStartToPlayhead(_:))
428	            ),
429	            (
430	                "arrow.left.to.line", "⇤", "Trim End to Playhead (E)",
431	                #selector(EditorViewController.trimEndToPlayhead(_:))
432	            ),
433	            (
434	                "delete.left", "⌫", "Ripple Delete (⌘⌫)",
435	                #selector(EditorViewController.rippleDeleteClips(_:))
436	            ),
437	            ("bookmark", "◆", "Add Marker (M)", #selector(EditorViewController.addMarker(_:))),
438	            (
439	                "doc.on.doc", "⧉", "Duplicate (⌘D)",
440	                #selector(EditorViewController.duplicateClips(_:))
441	            ),
442	            ("textformat", "Aa", "Add Text (T)", #selector(EditorViewController.addTextClip(_:))),
443	            (
444	                "square.on.circle", "▭", "Add Shape",
445	                #selector(EditorViewController.showAddShapeMenu(_:))
446	            ),
447	        ]
448	        return items.map { symbol, fallback, tooltip, action in
449	            GhostButton(
450	                symbol: symbol, fallback: fallback, caption: nil, tooltip: tooltip,
451	                action: action, size: actionSize, pointSize: actionPointSize,
452	                cornerRadius: DS.buttonRadius)
453	        }
454	    }
455	
456	    /// − · slider · + · Fit. The magnifiers target the timeline directly
457	    /// because `EditorViewController.zoomIn(_:)` is the CANVAS zoom and the
458	    /// responder chain would hand them that one.
459	    ///
460	    /// Fit is not in the design's cluster, and is kept anyway: it is a real
461	    /// command with a menu item (⇧Z) and this button is its only one-click
462	    /// path.
463	    private static func zoomCluster(owner: TimelineView) -> NSView {
464	        let out = GhostButton(
465	            symbol: "minus.magnifyingglass", fallback: "−", caption: nil,
466	            tooltip: "Zoom Out", action: #selector(TimelineView.timelineZoomOut(_:)),
467	            size: actionSize, pointSize: 15, cornerRadius: DS.buttonRadius)
468	        out.target = owner
469	        let into = GhostButton(
470	            symbol: "plus.magnifyingglass", fallback: "+", caption: nil,
471	            tooltip: "Zoom In", action: #selector(TimelineView.timelineZoomIn(_:)),
472	            size: actionSize, pointSize: 15, cornerRadius: DS.buttonRadius)
473	        into.target = owner
474	
475	        // Spec §4.4's zoom SLIDER is the shared file's `BlockSlider`
476	        // (`Controls.swift`, Rasterize's, kept in sync): a 3 pt track and a
477	        // 7 × 11 pt block knob in place of the system knob.
478	        let slider = owner.zoomSlider
479	        slider.target = owner
480	        slider.action = #selector(TimelineView.zoomSliderChanged(_:))
481	        slider.isContinuous = true
482	        slider.controlSize = .small
483	        slider.toolTip = "Timeline Zoom"
484	        slider.widthAnchor.constraint(equalToConstant: 110).isActive = true
485	
486	        let fit = GhostButton(

522	/// The bar's left-edge identity block: a kind-tinted chip, the selected clip's
523	/// name, and the track and kind under it.
524	///
525	/// It is one of three views of one selection — the timeline's own outline and
526	/// the inspector's header are the others — so its chip, its word for a kind
527	/// and its tint all come from `ClipKindStyle` rather than being spelled again
528	/// here.
529	///
530	/// Its width is FIXED at the design's 176 pt minimum rather than growing with
531	/// the name: the point of the block is that the divider after it never moves,
532	/// so a long name truncates instead of pushing the tools sideways.
533	final class TimelineSelectionBlock: NSView {
534	    private var snapshot = ProjectSnapshot.empty
535	    private var selection: Set<UInt32> = []
536	
537	    private static let width: CGFloat = 176
538	    private static let chip = NSSize(width: 8, height: 20)
539	    private static let gap: CGFloat = 8
540	
541	    init() {
542	        super.init(frame: .zero)
543	    }
544	
545	    @available(*, unavailable)
546	    required init?(coder: NSCoder) {
547	        fatalError("TimelineSelectionBlock does not support NSCoder")
548	    }
549	
550	    override var isFlipped: Bool { true }
551	
552	    override var intrinsicContentSize: NSSize {
553	        NSSize(width: Self.width, height: 30)
554	    }
555	
556	    func update(snapshot: ProjectSnapshot, selection: Set<UInt32>) {
557	        self.snapshot = snapshot
558	        self.selection = selection
559	        needsDisplay = true
560	    }
561	
562	    /// The clips the block is describing, in timeline order.
563	    private var clips: [ClipSnapshot] {
564	        snapshot.clips.filter { selection.contains($0.id) }.sorted { $0.start < $1.start }
565	    }
566	
567	    /// Chip tint, headline and meta line for the current selection.
568	    ///
569	    /// The design covers none and one. For MANY the honest thing is the count
570	    /// plus whatever the clips still agree on: a shared track keeps its name
571	    /// and a shared kind keeps its word, and where they disagree the line says
572	    /// so ("3 tracks", "mixed") rather than naming one clip's and implying it
573	    /// holds for the rest.
574	    private func description() -> (tint: NSColor, name: String, meta: String) {
575	        let clips = self.clips
576	        guard let first = clips.first else {
577	            return (DS.borderStrong, "No selection", "")
578	        }
579	        let kinds = Set(clips.map { ClipKindStyle.name(for: $0, in: snapshot) })
580	        let tracks = Set(clips.map { $0.track })
581	        let kind = kinds.count == 1 ? ClipKindStyle.name(for: first, in: snapshot) : "mixed"
582	        let track =
583	            tracks.count == 1 ? trackName(first.track) : "\(tracks.count) tracks"
584	        guard clips.count > 1 else {
585	            return (
586	                ClipKindStyle.tint(for: first, in: snapshot), snapshot.name(of: first),
587	                "\(track) · \(kind)")
588	        }
589	        let tint = kinds.count == 1
590	            ? ClipKindStyle.tint(for: first, in: snapshot) : DS.borderStrong
591	        return (tint, "\(clips.count) clips", "\(track) · \(kind)")
592	    }
593	
594	    /// The label a track wears in the timeline — the header column's spelling,
595	    /// not a second one.
596	    ///
597	    /// `set_track` accepts an EMPTY name, so `track(_:)?.name` is not enough:
598	    /// an unnamed track would print as nothing at all here while
599	    /// `TimelineHeaderView.draw` shows it as "Track 3", and the block would be
600	    /// naming a row the user cannot find. The number is the MODEL index + 1,
601	    /// which is what the header counts (0 = back), never the display row.
602	    private func trackName(_ id: UInt32) -> String {
603	        guard let index = snapshot.trackIndex(of: id) else { return "Track" }
604	        let name = snapshot.tracks[index].name
605	        return name.isEmpty ? "Track \(index + 1)" : name
606	    }
607	
608	    override func draw(_ dirtyRect: NSRect) {
609	        let content = description()
610	        let chip = NSRect(
611	            x: 0, y: (bounds.height - Self.chip.height) / 2,
612	            width: Self.chip.width, height: Self.chip.height)
613	        content.tint.setFill()
614	        chip.fill()
615	
616	        let textX = chip.maxX + Self.gap
617	        let textWidth = max(bounds.width - textX, 0)
618	        guard textWidth > 8 else { return }
619	        // The two lines are centred as a PAIR — 13 pt of name, 2 pt, 11 pt of
620	        // meta — so the block sits on the bar's centre line whatever height
621	        // the stack view hands it, and an empty meta line does not leave the
622	        // name floating high.
623	        let hasMeta = !content.meta.isEmpty
624	        let block: CGFloat = hasMeta ? 26 : 13
625	        let top = ((bounds.height - block) / 2).rounded()
626	        TimelineDraw.truncated(
627	            content.name,
628	            in: CGRect(x: textX, y: top, width: textWidth, height: 13),
629	            font: DS.sans(11, weight: .semibold), color: DS.textStrong)
630	        guard hasMeta else { return }
631	        TimelineDraw.truncated(
632	            content.meta,
633	            in: CGRect(x: textX, y: top + 15, width: textWidth, height: 11),
634	            font: DS.mono(9), color: DS.textFaint)
635	    }
636	}

4	/// The Media tab (spec §4.3): every imported file with its thumbnail, name,
5	/// duration, dimensions, rate and badges; Add Media… (⇧⌘I); Finder drops onto
6	/// the panel; a drag from a row to a timeline track or onto the canvas; the
7	/// find band road map 2's phase 8c added — a search, a sort and an "unused
8	/// only" switch (`MediaListFilter.swift`) — and the row menu: Insert at
9	/// Playhead, Overwrite at Playhead, Reveal in Timeline, Reveal in Finder,
10	/// Relink…, Remove.
11	///
12	/// There is no left panel in this app (§11), so this list IS the library.
13	/// Files are referenced, never copied (path + bookmark, §11), which is why a
14	/// row can be "missing" and why Relink… lives here.
15	///
16	/// **The find band does not rebuild the pane, and that is the whole design of
17	/// it.** `InspectorPaneView.rebuild()` removes every arranged subview and
18	/// asks `makeSections()` for a new set, `InspectorViewController.refresh` runs
19	/// it whenever `structureSignature` changes, and nothing in the inspector
20	/// preserves the first responder across one — so a search field built inside
21	/// `makeSections()` with the filtered set in the signature would be destroyed
22	/// by the first keystroke that changed the list, taking the field editor and
23	/// the caret with it (measured: removing a text field's ancestor leaves
24	/// `currentEditor()` nil and the window itself as first responder). So the
25	/// signature stays what it always was — a statement about the MODEL's shape —
26	/// and `arrange()` applies the search, the sort and the switch to the rows
27	/// that are already built, by hiding and re-ordering the list stack's
28	/// arranged subviews. Both are measured, not assumed: an `isHidden` arranged
29	/// subview leaves an `NSStackView`'s layout entirely (four 20 pt rows measure
30	/// 89 pt, three of them 66), and `insertArrangedSubview(_:at:)` MOVES a view
31	/// that is already arranged rather than duplicating it (the subview count
32	/// does not change) while leaving the window's first responder and the
33	/// caret's offset exactly where they were.
34	final class MediaPane: InspectorPaneView {
35	    override var tab: InspectorTab { .media }
36	
37	    /// The Media tab always has something to show — including when there is
38	    /// nothing imported yet, which is when Add Media… matters most.
39	    override var emptyMessage: String? { nil }
40	
41	    /// The rows, in the order the model lists them, each with the id it
42	    /// draws. The id is kept beside the view rather than read back off it so
43	    /// that `arrange()` can look the CURRENT entry up in the snapshot: a
44	    /// relink changes a file's name without changing this pane's signature,
45	    /// and a cached `MediaSnapshot` would sort and search against the name
46	    /// the row no longer shows.
47	    ///
48	    /// Internal rather than private for one caller: `select(_:)` redraws them
49	    /// and lives in `MediaPaneCommands.swift`, which is where the row's seven
50	    /// commands went when this file crossed the size cap. That is the whole
51	    /// cost of the split.
52	    var rows: [(media: UInt32, view: MediaRowView)] = []
53	
54	    /// The find band's state. View state, not persisted, and not part of the
55	    /// signature below — `MediaListFilter` argues both.
56	    private var filter = MediaListFilter()
57	
58	    /// The three things `arrange()` changes without a rebuild. Weak, because
59	    /// the view hierarchy owns them and a rebuild replaces all three;
60	    /// `InspectorPaneView.rebuild()` holds the previous generation one build
61	    /// longer, so a stale strong reference here would outlive the pane's own
62	    /// rule about that.
63	    private weak var listStack: NSStackView?
64	    private weak var tallyLabel: InspectorRowLabel?
65	    private weak var noMatchesRow: NSView?
66	
67	    /// The order `arrange()` last put the rows in, so it can leave the stack
68	    /// alone when nothing has moved — it runs on every refresh, and a live
69	    /// canvas drag refreshes this panel thirty times a second.
70	    private var arrangedOrder: [UInt32] = []
71	
72	    /// The MODEL's shape: which media exist and whether each one's file is
73	    /// there. Deliberately says nothing about the search text, the sort or
74	    /// the unused-only switch — see the class doc: putting the filtered set
75	    /// in here is precisely the bug this pane is built to avoid.
76	    override var structureSignature: String {
77	        // `:c` for a media with a cursor file: a Locate… or a Remove adds or
78	        // drops it, so the Cursor section's rows are rebuilt (CU-54).
79	        let media = binding.snapshot.media.map { entry -> String in
80	            "\(entry.id):\(mediaURL(for: entry) == nil ? "missing" : "ok")"
81	                + (entry.cursor == nil ? "" : ":c")
82	        }
83	        return "media|" + media.joined(separator: ",")
84	    }
85	
86	    override init(inspector: InspectorViewController) {
87	        super.init(inspector: inspector)
88	        // Finder drops land on the panel (§4.3). The editor's root view takes
89	        // file drops too, but it OPENS them as documents; a drop on this
90	        // panel means "add to this project", so the pane claims the type
91	        // first by being the deeper registered view.
92	        registerForDraggedTypes([.fileURL])
93	        NotificationCenter.default.addObserver(
94	            self, selector: #selector(cacheChanged(_:)), name: .mediaCacheDidChange, object: nil)
95	    }
96	
97	    @available(*, unavailable)
98	    required init?(coder: NSCoder) {
99	        fatalError("MediaPane does not support NSCoder")
100	    }
101	
102	    deinit {
103	        NotificationCenter.default.removeObserver(self)
104	    }
105	
106	    // MARK: - Sections
107	
108	    /// The redesign makes this tab a real LIST rather than a stack of button
109	    /// rows (handoff README, Part 2 §5): a 38 pt action row, the rows 3 pt
110	    /// apart, and a 40 pt footer carrying Consolidate… and one line saying
111	    /// what it does. It is still ONE `InspectorSection`, because the panel's
112	    /// shell builds every pane from sections and this one has no business
113	    /// forking that.
114	    override func makeSections() -> [InspectorSection] {
115	        rows = []
116	        listStack = nil
117	        noMatchesRow = nil
118	        arrangedOrder = []
119	        var content: [NSView] = [actionRow()]
120	        if binding.snapshot.media.isEmpty {
121	            // No find band with nothing to find: the band would be three dead
122	            // controls over a line saying the list is empty, and the pane is
123	            // rebuilt the moment the first file lands.
124	            content.append(
125	                inspectorRow(nil, [InspectorRowLabel("Drop files here, or use Add Media….")]))
126	        } else {
127	            content.append(findRow())
128	            content.append(listView())
129	            content.append(noMatchesView())
130	        }
131	        content.append(footerRow())
132	        // The rows exist and the band's controls hold the state, so the
133	        // filter can be applied to this build before it is ever shown — which
134	        // is what carries a search across the rebuild an import causes.
135	        arrange()
136	        let files = InspectorSection(id: "media.files", title: "Media", rows: content)
137	        // Camera Log (spec §11 GR-16) acts on a video file, so it is there
138	        // once the project has one (`MediaPane+CameraLog.swift`); HDR10 (spec
139	        // §11 HD-12) on a PQ file, once the project has one
140	        // (`MediaPane+HDR10.swift`); Cursor (spec §11 CU-54) on a video with a
141	        // picture, once the project has one (`MediaPane+Cursor.swift`).
142	        let media = binding.documentSnapshot.media
143	        let video = media.contains { $0.kind == .video }
144	        let pq = media.contains { $0.color?.pq != nil }
145	        let cursor = MediaPane.showsCursorSection(media)
146	        return (video ? [files, cameraLogSection()] : [files]) + (pq ? [hdr10Section()] : [])
147	            + (cursor ? [cursorSection()] : [])
148	    }
149	
150	    /// Add Media…, its ⇧⌘I hint, and the item count at the trailing edge.
151	    ///
152	    /// The count used to be a plain label built once per rebuild, because it
153	    /// changed only when the media list did. It changes with the FILTER now —
154	    /// "3 of 40 items" is the one line that stops a narrowed list reading as a
155	    /// lost library — so the label is held and `arrange()` writes it. It is
156	    /// still not an `OptionControl`: those read the model, and this reads the
157	    /// pane's own view state.
158	    private func actionRow() -> NSView {
159	        let add = commandButton(
160	            "Add Media…", #selector(EditorViewController.addMediaFiles(_:)),
161	            toolTip: "Import files into this project (⇧⌘I)")
162	
163	        let count = binding.snapshot.media.count
164	        let label = MediaPane.caption(MediaPane.tally(shown: count, of: count))
165	        tallyLabel = label
166	        return MediaPane.bar(

273	    /// The search, the sort and the unused-only switch applied to the rows
274	    /// this pane already holds — no rebuild, so the field being typed into
275	    /// keeps its caret (the class doc says why that is the point).
276	    ///
277	    /// The order is applied to EVERY row and the hiding to every row
278	    /// separately: moving a row and hiding one are different jobs, and a
279	    /// hidden row that keeps its place in the sort comes back where it
280	    /// belongs when the search is cleared. Nothing is written that does not
281	    /// have to be — this runs on every refresh, including a live gesture's
282	    /// thirty a second.
283	    private func arrange() {
284	        // The DOCUMENT's snapshot, and only one of the three things read off
285	        // it needs to be (road map 2's phase 9): `filter.admits` asks
286	        // `usesMedia`, and inside a nest a scoped view holds the NEST's clips
287	        // at top level and the timeline's nowhere — so a file used only by a
288	        // timeline clip would read as unused and "Unused only" would offer to
289	        // remove it. `media` itself is the same list either way (the view
290	        // carries the parent's `media[]` unchanged), so the order and the
291	        // tally are unaffected; this is written as one local so the question
292	        // cannot be asked two ways in one method.
293	        let snapshot = binding.documentSnapshot
294	        let order = filter.ordered(snapshot.media)
295	        if let stack = listStack, order != arrangedOrder {
296	            var index = 0
297	            for id in order {
298	                guard let row = rows.first(where: { $0.media == id })?.view else { continue }
299	                stack.insertArrangedSubview(row, at: index)
300	                index += 1
301	            }
302	            arrangedOrder = order
303	        }
304	        var shown = 0
305	        for row in rows {
306	            let visible = snapshot.media(row.media).map { filter.admits($0, in: snapshot) } ?? false
